questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a Master's student in Economics, I chose the University of Barcelona as my study destination because of its strong reputation in the field of economics, as well as the availability of programs that aligned with my interests. Additionally, I was attracted to the location of the university in the vibrant city of Barcelona, which offered unique cultural and professional opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although I really enjoyed my exchange experience in Barcelona, the workload was more challenging than expected due to the need to complete six courses in only three months to achieve the necessary credits. While the pace was demanding, I appreciated the opportunity to immerse myself in my studies and found the experience to be valuable overall.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: One challenge I encountered during my exchange experience in Barcelona was the difficulty in finding information due to the fact that some of the information resources were only available in Catalan without a translation. This made it more challenging to navigate some administrative processes, but I found that seeking out assistance from university staff and local resources was helpful in overcoming this obstacle.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We attended a intro presentation on the university. It was mainly directed towards students on the bachelor. It could have been nice with a more thorough intro to the masters program.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They honestly seemed a bit confused and the response time was quite slow. It was also very challenging to obtain information on grading and the exams.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for us to find housing, since we were four student and already knew each other from the University of Copenhagen, therefore we were able to rent an airbnb together which reduces costs compared to renting on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is important to do some research on the different areas in Barcelona. Also on the travel time to school.- Some areas can be a bit scary in the evening.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I actually did not do any research on housing through the university, so I do not know. And we did know receive any information about it from the school, but I have heard from other exchange students in Barcelona that it was quite expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easier, however there were some confusing about the insurance papers and what they thought they did or did not receive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to print a lot of document beforehand. This includes insurance document, passport documents and so on. When we were there we also had to select the courses we wanted to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were able to ask the staff questions, but they did not really know much about the master that we took

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful I guess

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are able to, write the university beforehand and see if you can get more information on the specific classes than what you can find online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teachers were really good, but again the workload was quite large.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the level of the courses was for some of the courses a bit below but with larger workload and for other of the courses the same level as my home institution or a bit above. It differs a lot for both institutions, so it is difficult to compare.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes at the University of Barcelona differs in a way that I really appreciated by having more intimate class sizes, which allowed for more discussion and participation among students. With fewer students in each class, there was more opportunity for engagement and interaction, which made the learning experience more engaging and dynamic. Also the teachers were more welcoming to discussions after class and had open office hours were we often went by to get guidance and help with assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: cooperative decision making and social choice - which is a course in game theory. If one enjoys micro economics this class is really interesting and the teacher is extremely good at teaching it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I do not think any items were more or less expensive. But it is smart to by a three months metro ticket to begin with or else metro expenses can be high - however, this is nothing compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in any of them. I did participate in some of the erasmus parties and trips, but I do not know if this counts? They were really good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, because I did not do any of them. I think there were some sports activities but with the amount of school hours we had, this would not have been possible to participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Did not do any so I cannot recommend anything.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on erasmus trips. They have some to different cities and also some sunday trips were you go on hikes or go sailing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me to adjust to the local culture during my exchange experience in Barcelona. I found the city and its people to be welcoming and friendly, and I appreciated the opportunity to immerse myself in a new culture and way of life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Erasmus events are an excellent way to get to know other students on exchange and meet new people while studying abroad. They provide opportunities to socialize and engage with others from diverse backgrounds. It is a bit more difficult to get to know local students but one way is by doing projects with people from your classes and invite them about for drinks and beers after.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No not really - as a said before, I find the people in Barcelona really welcoming. However, if you are a person which likes to arrive on time, you might find it difficult to adjust to "spanish time".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I particularly appreciated the local culture and cuisine. I loved exploring the city's vibrant food scene, trying new dishes like paella and tapas, and experiencing the social aspect of eating together with friends. Additionally, I enjoyed learning about the city's rich cultural history through visiting museums, attending cultural events, and exploring architectural landmarks such as the Gothic Quarter. I also do like the chill mentally of the people of Barcelona

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Embrace the local culture - Barcelona has a unique and vibrant culture that is different from what you may be used to in Denmark. Try to immerse yourself in the local culture by learning the language, trying new foods, and attending cultural events. You will have a much richer experience if you embrace the city's unique identity.
2. Make an effort to meet people- Studying abroad is an incredible opportunity to meet people from all over the world. Don't be afraid to introduce yourself to other exchange students and locals, and take advantage of opportunities to participate in social events and activities organized by Erasmus.
3. Stay organized and plan ahead - It's important to stay organized, keep track of deadlines when you have a lot of courses BUT remember to enjoy the city at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes, I would probably recommend not taking as many courses as I did or spread it out over a longer period

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was living in the vibrant city of Barcelona. I enjoyed immersing myself in the local culture, exploring the city's many sights and attractions, and meeting people from all over the world. The experience challenged me to step outside of my comfort zone and broaden my perspective, and I came away with a newfound appreciation for the diversity and richness of the world around us

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: living with friends. We lived in a quite small apartment and in periods during exams and so on, it could be a bit difficult not to have your own space however it was also a great experience to live with friends and I would do it again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
